item.title: A prime-editing-based strategy for pooled protein tagging and subcellular localization mapping.
item.abstract: The subcellular organization of proteins carries important information on cell state and gene function, yet there are limited technologies that enable routine measurements of protein localization at scale. Here we develop pooled endogenous protein tagging using prime editing to image subcellular localizations for many proteins in parallel within a heterogeneous cell pool. We constructed three prime editing libraries comprising 17,280 prime editing guide RNAs (pegRNAs) to exhaustively tag 60 endogenous proteins spanning diverse localization patterns and explore a broad space of genomic and pegRNA design parameters. We integrate pegRNA features into a predictive computational model for tagging efficiency to constrain the search space of effective pegRNAs for large-scale peptide knock-in. Last, we show that combining in situ pegRNA sequencing with deep learning image analysis enables scalable exploration of subcellular organization, setting the stage for systematic studies of proteome dynamics across cell types and perturbations.

item.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
item.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli, or yeast, whereas only a subset of engineering strategies has been validated directly in plants, including soybean hairy roots, rice, and Populus. This mini-review summarizes the latest research progress of AI in the field of Cas12 protein optimization and functional prediction, discusses the opportunities and challenges in its application in plants, and provides new ideas for future AI-driven plant gene editing.

item.title: Selective suppression and biasing of chemokine receptors CCR9 and ACKR4 through targeting CCL25 with de novo miniproteins.
item.abstract: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts target the receptors, whereas natural regulatory mechanisms modulate immune responses by directly binding to or modifying the chemokine ligands. Despite this insight, development of effective chemokine-directed modulators has remained elusive. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer an unprecedented opportunity to produce high-affinity binders that efficiently block protein-protein interactions. We implemented a computational workflow leveraging the BindCraft platform to generate miniprotein binders against CCL25, the chemokine ligand for the receptors CCR9 and ACKR4, and implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases. The unbiased development results in several miniproteins designed to block the receptor N-terminus from wrapping the chemokine and preventing productive engagement. Thus, these proteins suppress CCL25-mediated effector coupling and halt MOLT-4 lymphoblast migration. Another class of miniprotein, represented by VUP25111, is predicted to bind CCL25 along the chemokine β1 strand and retained receptor binding. This complex inhibited arrestin recruitment to CCR9, but not to ACKR4, indicating receptor specificity. Additionally, G protein recruitment to CCR9 was unimpeded by VUP25111, suggesting that the miniprotein biased the native agonist towards G proteins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of differentially targeting CCL25 to suppress CCR9 signaling and new tools to resolve the structural basis of chemokine receptor activation and bias.

item.title: Optimization of the pC-HSL-Induced Transcriptional Regulator, Rpa, for Use in Plant Synthetic Biology.
item.abstract: Advancements in plant synthetic biology rely on developing genetic parts with reliable and tunable expression levels for regulation of large genetic pathways. A slow design-build-test cycle and vast design space for modifying genetic parts make precise development of plant synthetic biology tools a challenge. In this work, a transcriptional activator derived from Rhodopseudomonas palustris and re-tooled to function in plants was optimized for low basal expression and high activated expression upon induction with the ligand p-Coumaroyl-homoserine lactone. Modifications to the activation domain, nuclear localization signal, DNA operator design, minimal promoter driving the reporter gene, and combinatorial pairings of these modifications resulted in significant variation in the dynamic range of the system. The overall lowest basal expression produced from the tested designs was approximately 30% that of the internal reference gene elongation factor-1 α and the greatest activated expression produced was approximately 130-fold induction. Functionality of expression from the optimized activation system was demonstrated in both transient Nicotiana benthamiana assays and stably transformed potato, with successful induction observed from a range of concentrations and application methods of p-Coumaroyl-homoserine lactone.

item.title: Synthetic consortia for organic pollutant bioremediation: integrating ecological design, synthetic biology, and machine learning.
item.abstract: Refractory organic contaminants pose a severe environmental threat because their complete mineralization often demands multi-step biochemical pathways, intermediate detoxification, and sustained microbial viability across variable microenvironments. While bioremediation provides a green alternative to physicochemical remediation, single isolates and empirically assembled co-cultures frequently suffer from pathway bottlenecks, metabolic stress, and environmental instability. Synthetic biology addresses these shortfalls by enabling targeted pathway refactoring, chassis optimization, and synthetic cell-cell interaction networks. Here, we outline a unified framework for engineering pollutant-degrading microbial consortia. We analyze foundational biodegradation databases, chassis-selection parameters, genetic-editing tools, and ecological assembly rules that sustain division of labor. We further assess how machine-learning platforms streamline member selection and community optimization, while emphasizing that predictive models demand validation through empirical degradation kinetics and multi-omics profiling. Finally, we highlight key technical hurdles to field deployment, focusing on genetic stability, biocontainment, long-term functional persistence, and environmental adaptability.

item.title: Engineered Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm beyond Conventional Biomaterials.
item.abstract: Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

item.title: Challenges and opportunities in antimicrobial R&D.
item.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is accelerating, while the discovery and development of new drugs, particularly those with novel mechanisms of action, have failed to keep pace. This widening gap reflects two major challenges: insufficient resources for antibiotic discovery and clinical development, and a lack of scientific innovation. With pharmaceutical companies largely abandoning antibiotic R&D, academic groups, small biotech companies, and not-for-profits are stepping in, harnessing advances in genomics, synthetic biology, and AI to drive discovery. Coupled with growing international investment and initiatives to address funding gaps, these efforts offer renewed hope for overcoming the antimicrobial resistance crisis.

item.title: The dual role of Fusobacterium nucleatum in colorectal cancer: from oncogenic mechanisms to immunotherapy sensitization.
item.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) has emerged as a critical microbial modulator in the development, progression, and therapeutic response of colorectal cancer (CRC). High-resolution genomic evidence identifies Fn subsp. animalis Clade 2 (Fna C2) as the predominant clade enriched in tumor microenvironments and invasive biofilms, favored by Fna C2-specific metabolic adaptations (utilizing ethanolamine and 1,2-propanediol) and a glutamate-dependent acid resistance (GDAR) system. At the molecular level, Fn drives oncogenesis, inflammation, and metastasis via the FadA/β-catenin and Fap2/TIGIT pathways, as well as the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/MyD88/NF-κB/microRNA-21 (miR-21) axis that suppresses RAS GTPase-activating protein 1 (RASA1) to hyperactivate RAS signaling. Fap2-mediated invasion further triggers interleukin-8 (IL-8) and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CXCL1) secretion, recruiting myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and neutrophils to foster a pro-tumor niche. Additionally, Fn confers chemoresistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) through BIRC3 (an inhibitor of apoptosis protein) upregulation and autophagy pathways. Paradoxically, Fn also acts as a "double-edged sword" by sensitizing microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This immunosensitization is mediated via a dual pathway: cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-STING activation enhancing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and microbial butyrate acting as a histone deacetylase 3/8 (HDAC3/8) inhibitor to epigenetically reprogram CD8+ T cells against exhaustion. To address the spatial heterogeneity and the safety risks of live bacterial therapy, translational efforts are pivoting toward cell-free interventions such as postbiotics and STING agonists. This review comprehensively delineates the clade-specific traits of Fna C2 alongside broader Fn immunomodulatory mechanisms, highlighting its potential and current limitations as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in precision CRC care.

item.title: Astrocyte Membrane-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles with Hypoxia-Remodeled Cargo Attenuate Reactive Astrocyte Programs and Promote Spinal Cord Repair.
item.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) represent promising cell-free therapeutics for spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by variable cargo potency and insufficient cell-selective delivery. Here, we developed a modular biomimetic vesicle platform integrating hypoxic remodeling of mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEV (MSC-sEV) cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering. In a rat model of SCI, hypoxia-preconditioned MSC-sEVs (Hyp-sEVs) attenuated C3-positive astrocyte reactivity and improved functional outcomes. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses identified ERBIN as a key therapeutic cargo enriched in Hyp-sEVs that contributed to suppression of the NOD2/IRF3/GBP1 signaling axis. To enhance astrocyte-directed delivery, Hyp-sEVs were fused with astrocyte-derived membranes to generate astrocyte membrane-engineered vesicles (A-EVs). A-EVs were preferentially taken up by astrocytes, and blocking and knockdown experiments implicated MERTK and the ligands PROS1/GAS6 in this uptake. A-EVs outperformed Hyp-sEVs in preserving spinal cord tissue and promoting functional recovery. Together, these findings indicate that coupling hypoxia-remodeled sEV cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering promotes preferential vesicle uptake by astrocytes, attenuates C3-positive astrocyte reactivity, and improves functional recovery after SCI in rats.

item.title: From the bench to the bedside: mesenchymal stromal cells as immunoregulatory and regenerative therapies.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as one of the most extensively studied adult stem cell populations, celebrated for their self-renewal, multilineage differentiation potential, and remarkable immunomodulatory properties. Originally discovered in bone marrow, MSCs are now known to reside in diverse tissues and have transitioned from experimental therapies to clinical applications for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), autoimmune disorders, and regenerative medicine. However, despite the approval of several MSC products, enthusiasm is tempered by persistent challenges, including biological heterogeneity and inconsistent clinical efficacy.
MAIN BODY: This review comprehensively examines current knowledge on MSCs, evaluating their translational trajectory from preclinical discovery to clinical application. We first examine their biological foundations and molecular mechanisms, with a specific focus on paracrine signaling, extracellular vesicles-mediated effects, and the purinergic signaling axis. We then systematically assess their clinical applications across immune-mediated diseases, musculoskeletal disorders, and neurological conditions. Crucially, we analyze the "efficacy-expectation gap" between robust preclinical results and variable clinical outcomes, identifying key translational barriers such as donor variability, manufacturing standardization, and safety concerns regarding tumor progression.
CONCLUSION: MSCs represent a clinically promising yet biologically complex modality in modern medicine. While they offer undeniable therapeutic promise, realizing their full potential requires resolving fundamental uncertainties in biology and standardization. Future directions lie in the development of engineered MSCs, cell-free EVs therapeutics, and omics-driven precision applications. By integrating mechanistic insights with advanced biotechnology, MSCs can evolve from variable biologicals into reproducible, programmable agents for precision and regenerative medicine.

item.title: Prenatal Screening and Diagnostic Testing in the Era of Genomic Medicine.
item.abstract: Prenatal genetic testing has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past two decades. Powered by genomic medicine, carrier screening, cell-free DNA screening, chromosomal microarray, exome sequencing, and genome sequencing have augmented the ability of obstetric care clinicians to diagnose fetal chromosomal imbalances and single-gene disorders and counsel patients on the clinical implications. Carrier screening with gene panels can identify asymptomatic carriers of a multitude of conditions, whereas cell-free DNA screening allows greater detection of aneuploidy with lower false-positive rates than ever thought possible. Prenatal diagnostic testing no longer involves simply looking at the structure of chromosomes. Chromosomal microarray analysis is capable of precisely identifying small areas of genomic imbalance, providing insight into affected genes. Next-generation sequencing-based diagnostic tests-targeted gene panels, exome sequencing, and genome sequencing-enable the diagnosis of many monogenic disorders prenatally and can provide a diagnosis in up to 25% of additional pregnancies with structural fetal anomalies compared with chromosomal microarray alone. An understanding of these tests will help obstetric care clinicians discuss available screening and diagnostic prenatal genetic tests with patients and explain their benefits, caveats, limitations, and results.

item.title: Electrospun scaffolds for MSC-derived secretome delivery.
item.abstract: The mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC)-derived secretome is emerging as a promising cell-free therapeutic product for tissue repair and regeneration. It contains soluble proteins, growth factors, nucleic acids, and extracellular vesicles (EVs), whose combined activity supports angiogenesis, immunomodulation, cytoprotection, and extracellular matrix remodelling. However, the biological activity of these components can be compromised during processing, storage, scaffold loading, and release. This review examines electrospun scaffolds as delivery platforms for the MSC-derived secretome, with particular attention to EV preservation and analytical evaluation. Selected non-electrospun platforms are discussed as comparators to clarify the advantages and limitations of electrospun delivery systems. We discuss how polymer composition, solvent exposure, crosslinking, fibre architecture, and loading strategy affect cargo retention, release kinetics, and biological activity. Post-fabrication adsorption generally minimises processing-related exposure of labile components but often results in rapid release, whereas matrix incorporation, affinity-based immobilisation, and microsphere-assisted loading can prolong delivery while introducing additional risks to vesicle and protein stability. Preclinical studies across these scaffold platforms report beneficial effects in models of skin, bone, cartilage, nerve, periodontal, and cardiac repair, but comparisons remain limited by inconsistent secretome preparation, dose reporting, and analytical methods. Progress towards translation will require standardised characterisation of both soluble and vesicular fractions, dose normalisation to scaffold mass or area, functional potency assays, and validation in long-term, clinically relevant animal models. Together, these developments will enable more reproducible engineering of electrospun secretome-delivery systems and support their clinical translation.

item.title: Streptococcus salivarius K12 and Its Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles Alleviate 5-Fluorouracil-Associated Oral Mucosal Injury and Remodel Oral and Gut Microbiota.
item.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis involves epithelial injury, inflammation, delayed mucosal repair, and microbial dysbiosis. This study investigated whether live Streptococcus salivarius K12 and a K12-derived bacterial extracellular vesicle (BEV) preparation alleviate 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-associated oral mucosal injury.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: K12-derived BEVs were isolated and characterized, and live K12 or the BEV preparation was administered orally to male mice. The model combined systemic 5-FU exposure with local acetic acid-induced tongue injury. Oral mucosal repair, inflammatory transcript expression, and oral and fecal microbiota were evaluated.
RESULTS: Both interventions promoted wound healing and increased epithelial thickness and collagen deposition compared with the 5-FU group. In tongue tissue, live K12 significantly reduced Tnf and Il6 mRNA expression relative to the 5-FU group, whereas the reduction in Il1b was not statistically significant. The BEV preparation significantly reduced all three transcripts relative to the 5-FU group. 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed group-associated variation in oral and fecal microbial community structure. K12 and BEV treatment were associated with different descriptive patterns of microbial composition. Under the non-dose-matched regimens tested, the BEV preparation produced greater improvements than live K12 in selected repair- and inflammation-related outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support further investigation of K12-derived BEV preparations as a potential cell-free intervention for chemotherapy-associated oral mucosal injury.

item.title: Abundance of carboxylesterase 1 in liver tissue and plasma-derived extracellular vesicles: Considerations for model-informed precision dosing.
item.abstract:
AIMS: Precision dosing requires accounting for variability in drug elimination capacity. Liquid biopsy, based on cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), offers a minimally invasive approach to characterize hepatic enzymes. The present study extends this framework to carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), an important determinant of exposure to prodrugs and active drugs.
METHODS: Matched liver tissue and plasma from 29 liver cancer patients were processed to measure CES1 protein (tissue proteomics) and cfRNA (RNA-seq of plasma-derived EVs). Individualized physiologically based pharmacokinetic models were generated to test the feasibility of model-informed precision dosing of D-methylphenidate and oseltamivir.
RESULTS: CES1 cfRNA in plasma EVs (0.79 ± 0.62 reads per million [RPM]) was correlated with protein abundance in liver (942.98 ± 427.04 pmol/mg protein) from the colorectal liver metastasis cohort (Pearson's r = .57, p = .003, n = 25). Individual cfRNA measurements were projected into hepatic CES1 abundance-based dosing inputs for simulations. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the determinants of exposure variability were CES1 abundance for D-methylphenidate and renal function for oseltamivir carboxylate. Liquid biopsy-informed dosing improved precision for D-methylphenidate only modestly, with greater benefits anticipated in populations exhibiting wider CES1 expression variability (2.8-fold reduction in variability predicted over the CES1 population expression range). Renal function-based individualization fully restored precision and accuracy for oseltamivir carboxylate (1.0-fold relative to reference population exposure), compared with uniform dosing (1.6-fold).
CONCLUSIONS: The findings underscore that liquid biopsy and conventional physiological markers are complementary tools within a model-informed precision dosing framework, each most valuable when applied to the rate-limiting elimination pathway.

item.title: Pathogen-dependent diagnostic performance of plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing in HIV-associated opportunistic infections.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opportunistic infections (OIs) remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLWH), particularly in patients with advanced immunosuppression. Blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) has emerged as a rapid and minimally invasive approach for pathogen detection; however, its diagnostic performance may vary substantially across pathogens because of differences in microbial dissemination patterns and circulating microbial cell-free DNA (cfDNA) burden. The pathogen-dependent diagnostic characteristics of blood mNGS in HIV-associated opportunistic infections remain insufficiently defined.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed HIV-infected patients who underwent plasma mNGS testing for suspected opportunistic infections at a tertiary referral center between January 2020 and July 2025. Patients were classified according to a composite clinical reference standard into Talaromycosis (TM), tuberculosis (TB), Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), and other opportunistic infections. Pathogen-specific detection performance and false-negative and false-positive results were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 87 HIV-infected patients with opportunistic infections were included. Blood mNGS demonstrated high overall pathogen detection sensitivity (91.46%) and positive predictive value (94.94%). Diagnostic performance differed markedly among pathogens. Blood mNGS showed excellent sensitivity for disseminated fungal infections, including TM (97.73%) and PJP (93.33%), whereas sensitivity was lower for TB (86.67%) and other localized or intracellular infections (62.50%). False-negative results predominantly occurred in infections characterized by tissue compartmentalization or low circulating microbial burden, including cryptococcal meningitis and Mycobacterium avium complex infection. In contrast, false-positive Pneumocystis detections likely reflected colonization or low-level microbial translocation rather than invasive disease.
CONCLUSION: The diagnostic performance of blood mNGS in HIV-associated opportunistic infections is strongly pathogen-dependent. Disseminated infections associated with high circulating microbial cfDNA burden demonstrate superior blood-based detection sensitivity, whereas localized or intracellular infections remain diagnostically challenging. These findings provide a biologically informed framework for interpreting blood mNGS results in immunocompromised patients and support the role of blood mNGS as a rapid adjunctive diagnostic tool in HIV-associated opportunistic infections.

cards.title_cn: 七年征程 十三亿同行——医保码激活使用人数超13亿

key_findings: 截至2026年10月底，全国医保码激活使用人数突破13亿。

颁奖仪式于11月25日在北京展览馆举行，集中展示医保数字化最新成果。

item.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
item.abstract: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.

cards.score_reason: GPT-6蛋白质设计突破，直接相关
cards.title_cn: GPT-6 模型展现内在蛋白质设计能力
cards.one_liner: GPT-6 通过推理与代码设计蛋白质结构与序列，实验验证可结合五个靶点。
key_findings: GPT-6 无需专门训练，凭推理与代码即可设计蛋白质结构与序列
实验室测试显示，设计蛋白对五个靶点均出现结合证据
能力来自通用模型本身，而非蛋白质专用模型
cards.why_it_matters: 通用大模型直接介入蛋白质设计，可能改变合成生物学中酶与结合蛋白的研发流程，值得评估其设计可靠性与可复现性。

item.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
item.abstract: Huang’s allies enlisted Trump and Vance to pressure Nvidia’s board into taking him back.

cards.score_reason: 英伟达高层政治博弈，重要
cards.title_cn: 特朗普与硅谷施压，英伟达董事会重新接纳黄仁勋
cards.one_liner: 黄仁勋盟友借特朗普与万斯向英伟达董事会施压，迫使其重新接纳黄仁勋。
key_findings: 黄仁勋的盟友联合特朗普与万斯，向英伟达董事会施加政治压力。
董事会最终让步，重新接纳黄仁勋回归。
事件凸显政治力量对科技公司治理的直接干预。
cards.why_it_matters: 英伟达是AI算力核心供应商，其治理稳定性影响GPU供应与AI研发节奏；合成生物学依赖AI与算力，需关注其战略连续性。

item.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
item.abstract: The Cairn AI framework is proving to be a boon for defenders and attackers.

cards.score_reason: AI智能体攻防，有明确价值
cards.title_cn: 亚马逊称黑客AI代理几乎无需人工介入即发现并利用0-day漏洞
cards.one_liner: 亚马逊披露黑客AI代理Cairn在极少人工介入下自主发现并利用0-day漏洞。
key_findings: Cairn AI框架对攻防双方均有助益，此次被用于攻击侧
AI代理几乎无需人工输入即完成0-day漏洞的发现与利用
该事件由亚马逊披露，凸显AI自动化漏洞挖掘的双用途风险
cards.why_it_matters: AI自主挖掘并利用0-day将压缩漏洞响应窗口，合成生物学实验室的自动化平台、LIMS与测序数据系统需提前评估此类AI驱动的攻击面。

item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.abstract: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.

cards.score_reason: AI辅助数学证明，值得关注

cards.one_liner: 一项新的 AI 辅助证明看起来可靠，但其真正含义尚不明确。
key_findings: 出现一项 AI 辅助的黎曼猜想相关证明，初步判断较为可靠
目前尚不清楚该证明究竟说明了什么，意义待厘清
cards.why_it_matters: 黎曼猜想是数学核心难题；AI 辅助证明若成立，将展示 AI 在基础数学中的潜力，但其实际价值仍需评估。

cards.one_liner: 保时捷 718 Boxster 纯电原型车完成试驾，确认驾驶乐趣，技术细节仍有限。

cards.one_liner: 纽约州立法禁止车企对加热座椅等硬件功能收取订阅费，2027年生效。
key_findings: 新法禁止将加热座椅等硬件功能设为付费订阅，2027年起在纽约州实施。
法律仍留有“持续成本”服务例外，被指为潜在漏洞。
该立法针对车企软件订阅收费模式，属消费者权益监管动向。
